Exercise 3.1 — RKHS continuity, Lipschitz constants and sharpness
      
        (a) Prove $|f(x)-f(x')|\le\|f\|_k\,d_k(x,x')$ with $d_k^2=k(x,x)-2k(x,x')+k(x',x')$ from the reproducing property. (b) For the SE kernel with length-scale $\ell$ show that every $f$ with $\|f\|_k\le B$ is $B/\ell$-Lipschitz. (c) For which $f$ is (a) an equality?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) By the reproducing property $f(x)-f(x')=\langle f,\varphi(x)\rangle_k-\langle f,\varphi(x')\rangle_k=\langle f,\varphi(x)-\varphi(x')\rangle_k$. Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|f(x)-f(x')|\le\|f\|_k\|\varphi(x)-\varphi(x')\|_k$, and $\|\varphi(x)-\varphi(x')\|_k^2=\langle\varphi(x),\varphi(x)\rangle_k-2\langle\varphi(x),\varphi(x')\rangle_k+\langle\varphi(x'),\varphi(x')\rangle_k=k(x,x)-2k(x,x')+k(x',x')$.
            (b) For the SE kernel $k(x,x)=1$ and $d_k^2=2\big(1-e^{-r^2/(2\ell^2)}\big)$ with $r=\|x-x'\|$. Since $1-e^{-a}\le a$ for $a\ge0$, $d_k^2\le r^2/\ell^2$, hence $|f(x)-f(x')|\le(\|f\|_k/\ell)\,r\le(B/\ell)\,r$. (Note the constant depends only on $B$ and $\ell$, never on the data, and that $d_k\le\sqrt2$ always: for far-apart points the RKHS bound is better than the Lipschitz bound.)
            (c) If $\varphi(x)=\varphi(x')$, both sides are zero for every $f$. Otherwise Cauchy–Schwarz is tight iff $f$ is a multiple of $\varphi(x)-\varphi(x')=k(x,\cdot)-k(x',\cdot)$; for that $f$ the two evaluations differ by exactly $\|f\|_kd_k(x,x')$. So no continuity argument can improve the lemma without extra assumptions.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: (a) Genuine reproducing identity, inner-product difference, Cauchy-Schwarz and exact kernel-distance-square expansion.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The actual RKHS section inner product evaluates f. Inner subtraction and real Cauchy-Schwarz prove the exact absolute bound. Actual norm-square expansion identifies d_k squared with the printed three kernel entries, in their symmetric real orientation.
hypotheses: A real genuine Mathlib RKHS of scalar functions is used: complete real Hilbert space with the actual reproducing sections RKHS.kerFun. The feature formulas are instantiated at those sections, not arbitrary unrelated vectors.

The SE kernel here has unit amplitude and a positive length-scale ell, the ordinary length-scale domain. B bounds the RKHS norm itself; nonnegativity B follows from that actual norm bound. Euclidean distance is the source r; the formal theorem also permits arbitrary pseudometric input domains.

The equality in(a)/(c) is the displayed ABSOLUTE evaluation difference. For coincident sections it is0 for every f. Otherwise every real scalar multiple of the section difference (including negative and zero multiples) attains equality; no claim of a signed positive difference is made.

Far-apart is the scoped comparison r/ell>sqrt2: the capped kernel-distance bound is then smaller than the unbounded distance factor in the Lipschitz estimate. With zero function/B both numeric error bounds may be0; the source describes an upper-bound comparison, not strict improvement for every zero function.
No observed data enter the derived constant B/ell. No general prior sampling, posterior confidence, RKHS construction theorem, or concentration law is inferred from this particular exercise.
